rv.q: They have every right to beam as this production, which is surely Broadway-bound, constitutes a thrilling shot in the arm for the much-loved musical with its divinely tuneful score.
And above all, it’s an absolute blast.
This ranks as an all-time great revival.
Prepare to be blown away by Rachel Zegler.
Rachel Zegler is an absolute smash in Jamie Lloyd’s thrilling revival of Andrew Lloyd Webber and Tim Rice’s improbable hit musical about Argentina’s populist, postwar first lady Eva Perón.
This gorgeous sensory overload of a show is its own comment on the rising tide of fascism.
This Evita is simply sensational.
It’s stunning: the apex of a show that, like Lloyd’s Sunset Boulevard, boldly reframes a much-loved musical for today.
It’s a pitch-perfect mix of theatrical audacity, political satire and deft cinematography.
Her voice brought the people to their feet.
If you feel denied of the subtleties of story, character and commentary on populist power, you will still have an eye-popping night out.
All credit to the hip young director for having the audacity to smack down the fourth wall.
Fabian Aloise’s thundering choreography is dead impressive, but it all feels like a hollow rock gig with a camera stunt attached.

This Evita might be regarded as the apotheosis of Lloyd’s mid-period style and Andrew Lloyd Webber and Tim Rice should be down on their knees thanking him for allowing their strongest, darkest show, first seen in 1978, to gleam with diamond-sharp brilliance.
This darkly brilliant Evita is bursting with star quality.

In my case, I emerged breathless with admiration, whilst also brooding upon the darker recesses arrived at this time round by material that had never before felt so, well, modern – sensual and scary, the two conjoined to intoxicating effect.
The energy of the 30-strong ensemble is often exhausting to watch, and there is little respite in the first half for either them or the audience!
In the hands of Alan Williams, the score sounds superb, and with such a talented cast delivering the goods, I have no doubt this version of Evita will become high flying adored.

It’s an updating which doesn’t always land the right historical tone, (Christian Dior would certainly raise an eyebrow) but as a piece of modern entertainment, it ticks far too many modern boxes to fail.
It is an exercise in meta-kitsch, and, on those terms, it succeeds.
But while it delivers in spades for the sensation-generation, something major is missing.
It's entertaining and galling in equal measure.
There's spectacle, star-power and emotion to complement some good songs, albeit too many done too loud and too fast.
It's more a drama-school showcase than an epic human tragedy.
The result is theatre at its very best.
This is not just a great production of Evita but one of the most exciting musicals I have witnessed in years.
Jamie Lloyd’s latest production is nothing short of a theatrical lightning strike – raw, visceral, and unrelentingly alive.
This production of Evita is, without a doubt, the show of the summer.
Technically brilliant, emotionally not so much.
Rachel Zegler’s performance as Eva Peron will be remembered and will elevate her star even higher.
This musical’s boldness is exactly what makes it exhilarating: an unapologetically big, loud, and brazen production that mirrors its protagonist’s boundless audacity.
Fabian Aloise’s choreography is a triumph.
Like a fever dream in a warehouse rave, yes.
And yet, I wasn’t alone in finding Evita hard work.
And having no emotional centre, this production leaves little impression — only a chill.
Let's just say it is absolutely the best show I have seen so far this year – and it will take a lot to top it.
It's raw, it's theatrical dynamite, and it couldn't feel more of the moment.
With Rachel Zegler’ s star turn anchoring it all, Evita just became the show of the summer.
Technically sublime, fiercely performed, and visually magnetic, it offers a fresh take on a classic and establishes Rachel Zegler as a theatrical force to be reckoned with.
Jamie Lloyd's revived Evita proves that star quality is no substitute for talent.

cn.t: Jamie Lloyd's bold, stripped-back Evita divides critics: many praise Rachel Zegler's phenomenal vocals and the electrifying balcony spectacle, while others find the rock-concert staging sacrifices narrative clarity for high-octane style over substance.

vr.q: If you like vibes based theater that takes you on an emotional journey, even though it can be a bit confusing at times, then I think you're gonna really love this production.
In spite of all of its shortcomings and all of its successes, it is regardless event theater which is not to be missed.
